newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks virtually flat at mid-session.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks virtually flat at mid-session.

text.p: Taiwan share prices remained virtually unchanged at mid-session on Thursday amid what brokers called a lack of market-inspiring factors.
With 90 minutes left, the weighted index was up a minuscule 0.31 points -- less than one-hundredth of a percent -- at 8,615.09.
Turnover was heavy at T$75.83 billion, but less active than the torrential volumes registered in recent sessions.
The market had opened lower on the government's announcement Wednesday that it would speed up its selldown of equity in the "Big Three" state-run commercial banks.
The Big Three -- First Bank, Hua Nan and Chang Hwa -- remained virtually unchanged after having fallen by over 10 percent each since their ex-rights date on April 10.
"They have already fallen a lot, so there is not much room for further drops," said Oliver Fang, an analyst for National Securities.
Brokers said the overall index likely would stay in a gradual downtrend due to the government's apparent reluctance to support the market at this time.
